FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Oils 
and Oilseeds Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. 

Chilli, Capsicum annuum, family Solanacaea, is extensively grown throughout India. The plant has many 
synonyms such as paprika, cayenne pepper, red pepper and capsicum in different parts of the world. Seeds 
are produced in considerable quantity in the process of making dry chillies. Presence of seeds is not 
desirable in chilli powder. 

The production of chillies in India probably exceeds 6 lakh tonnes per year. Taking the average seed 
content of 45 percent, the total seed would be over 2*7 lakh tonnes with an oil potential of around 
67 500 tonnes. The fatly acid composition of the oil is 73 percent Jinoleic acid, 8 percent oleic acid and 19 
percent saturated fatty acids. Absence of hnoleic acid is a factor favourable for chilhseed oil being used 
as a basic material in non-yellowing paints and surface coatings. 

Edible use of the refined oil is also not unlikely. However, specification for edible grade of chilliseed oil is 
yet to be included under the provisions of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and the Rules 
framed thereunder. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement ot this standard is complied with, the final 
value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or anal) sis, shall be rounded off in accordance 
with IS 2 : 1960 * Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )' The number of significant places 
retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard 



IS 13037 1 1991 



Indian Standard 
CHILLISEED OIL - SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

This standard prescribes requirements and 
methods of sampling and test for chilliseed oil. 

2 REFERENCES 

The following Indian Standards are necessary 
adjuncts to this standard:

3 TERMINOLOGY 

For the purpose of this standard, the definitions 
given in IS 11476 : 1985 shall apply. 

4 GRADES 

The material shall be of the following two grades: 

a) Raw, and 

b) Refined. 



5 REQUIREMENTS 
5.1 Description 



The material shall be obtained from clean and 
sound seeds of chilli ( Capsicum annuum ) It shall 
be clear and free from rancidity, adulterants, 
sediment, suspended and other foreign matter f 
separated water and added colouring substances. 

5-1.1 The clarity of the material shall be judged 
by the absence of turbidity after keeping the 
filtered sample at 30°C for 24 hours. 

5.2 Admixture with Other Oils 

5.2.1 The material shall be free from admixture 
of other oils and adulterants when tested accord- 
ing to the methods prescribed in IS 548 
( Part 2 ) : 1976 and Sections 9, and 21 of 
IS 548 ( Part 2 ). 

5.3 The material shall also comply with the 
requirements given in Table 1 . 

6 PACKING AND MARKING 

6.1 Packing 

The material shall be supplied in well-closed 
containers as agreed to between the purchaser 
and the supplier. 

6.2 Marking 

The containers shall be marked with the follow- 
ing information: 

a) Name and grade of the material, 

b) Net mass of the contents, 

c) Identification of the source of manufacture, 

d) Batch or lot number in code or otherwise > 
and 

e) Month and year of manufacture. 

7 SAMPLING 

7.1 Representative samples of the material shall 1 
be drawn as prescribed in 3 of IS 548 ( Part 1 ): 
1964. 

8 QUALITY OF REAGENTS 

8.1 Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals 
and distilled water ( see IS 1070 : 1977 ) shall 
be used in the tests. 

NOTE — 'Pure chemicals' shall mean chemicals that 
do not contain impurities which affect the results of 
analysis.

Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of (he Bureau of Indian Standards 
Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products 
covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply 
with the requirements of that standard und*T a well defined system of inspection, testing and 
quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard 
marked products are aiso continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a 
further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark 
may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of 
Indian Standards

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country.
